spec: Rule cards for libretro cores whose save behaviour deviates from RetroArch's standard savefile_directory rule. This is world knowledge under DESIGN.md's boundary rule: each card states WHICH live config governs the core and what its values mean — the current value is always read from the machine, never from here. A card states only what no read of the machine recovers: the .so name is derived from the card key and never restated, an option default is recorded only for a core that registers none (a probe of the binary reads the others), and what a card does state about the core's own vocabulary is machine-checked wherever a machine can check it. Cards are keyed by the core's canonical short name (the .so basename without _libretro.so, matching libretro-core-info filenames); 'identifiers' carries the display library_name the core binary reports, the one name that key does not give. 'saves.anchors' is that vocabulary's tripwire: every file name and subdir fragment a card records is pinned either to 'literal' — the whole NUL-delimited byte string the auditor read in the shipped .so, which a test re-reads there — or to an explicit reason no literal can carry it ('unprotected', the core composes the name at run time; 'arrangement', the path is one the arrangement builds and not the core's word at all). A recorded name with neither fails the tests; there is no silent opt-out. Facts live here; interpretation lives in code — a rule that does not fit this schema gets code plus a card referencing it, the schema does not grow a DSL. A declared file name may carry the placement's own hole tokens and nothing else (<rom_stem>, which the resolver fills from the content path, and <save_id>, which it never fills and hands to the caller as a hole); the loader refuses any other token, so a typo cannot travel into a filename atlas states as fact. The other closed vocabularies are the placement's too: 'root' and 'also_under' are savefile_directory | system_directory | content_directory (and a mode does not span its own root), 'granularity' is shared-card | per-game-file | per-game-files, and 'complete' must be a JSON boolean — never a quoted one, which Python would read as true. Format and per-field rules: atlas/data/README.md (shipped beside this file).

<rom_stem>.rtc.unprotected: composed at run time from the content's own stem and '.rtc' (program.cpp, the time.rtc branch). The whole string beside it in the binary is the resource name 'time.rtc', which is what the emulator asks its host for; the file it is answered with is named after the content

provenance.source: bsnes source at the version the shipped binary names (115). This core takes itself out of the libretro save interface deliberately and says so above the two functions: 'there is no safe/sensible way to use the memory interface without severe hackery. Rely on higan to load and save SRAM until there is really compelling reason not to' — retro_get_memory_data returns nullptr and retro_get_memory_size returns 0 for every id (bsnes/target-libretro/libretro.cpp:1037-1047), so RetroArch writes nothing at all. The core writes both files itself: its host resolves the emulator's 'save.ram' resource to <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.srm and 'time.rtc' to <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.rtc, both from GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY and both falling back to the content's own directory where the frontend names none (bsnes/target-libretro/program.cpp:503-530), and retro_unload_game calls the core's save() (libretro.cpp:1026-1030). Game Boy content, which this core is also launched for, takes the same two names through its own path (program.cpp:613-650). A cartridge without a clock is never asked for time.rtc, so the second name is an upper bound like every other file set here.

A record could state only the first of the two.

provenance.source: flycast_libretro.so option strings ('Per-Game VMUs', mode descriptions); live observation on RetroDECK 0.10.9b — <system_directory>/dc holds vmu_save_{A1,B1,C1,D1}.bin + dc_nvmem.bin, and a per-content run wrote <save_id>.<port>.bin for the four connected ports into the save directory the frontend handed the core. Names follow hostfs::getVmuPath (flycast@1dac369 shell/libretro/oslib.cpp:38-67): with settings.platform.isConsole() and a non-empty settings.content.gameId the name is that id — the disc's product number read from its header (core/emulator.cpp:838-841), trailing blanks trimmed, each of ' /\:*?|<>' replaced by '_' — and without one (arcade content, or a disc header stating none) the ROM's own name (oslib.cpp:62); a legacy ROM-named file is still read when no id-named one exists (oslib.cpp:55-60). The directory is RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY as the frontend redirected it (shell/libretro/libretro.cpp:2142-2148), so the mode nests no subdirectory of its own. Switching modes moves the save, it does not duplicate it: the shared cards stay behind untouched. Per-content applies per port — with 'VMU A1' only port A1 moves and B1..D1 keep using the shared card (oslib.cpp:40-41), which is why that mode states no file set. dc_nvmem.bin is the console's own flash, shared by every game in every mode, and stays under <system_directory>/dc throughout. That name is the core's own composition, not a string it stores: nvmem::loadFlash calls Load(getRomPrefix(), "%nvmem.bin", "nvram") and saveFiles calls Save(getRomPrefix(), "nvmem.bin", "nvmem") (core/hw/flashrom/nvmem.cpp:246, :305) — the read path replaces the '%' of a candidate entry with the prefix (hostfs::findFlash, shell/libretro/oslib.cpp:74-107, substitution at :91-93) and the write path prepends it unconditionally (hostfs::getFlashSavePath, :109-114). The candidate list holds that single entry, so no legacy spelling is read either. getRomPrefix() returns 'dc_' for DC_PLATFORM_DREAMCAST (nvmem.cpp:35-50), the one platform isConsole() covers (core/types.h:154) and the guard on both flash calls, which makes the naomi_/naomi2_/aw_ prefixes it can also return unreachable spellings for this file. Neither function consults reicast_per_content_vmus, and both root at game_dir_no_slash = <system_directory>/dc (shell/libretro/libretro.cpp:2140) — that is why the flash is shared in every mode while the VMUs move. Slot-2 VMUs (A2..D2) exist only when a port's slot 2 is configured as VMU; on Naomi the connected VMUs are B1 and C1 (core/hw/maple/maple_cfg.cpp:246-253). The key is reicast_per_content_vmus and not the flycast_per_content_vmus libretro's own documentation names (libretro/docs @ cf43d92 docs/library/flycast.md:294): every Flycast build prefixes its options with CORE_OPTION_NAME, which upstream still defines as "reicast" (flyinghead/flycast shell/libretro/libretro_core_option_defines.h:20, unchanged from the shipped 1dac369 to master a172e00) — the documented spelling is a docs bug, never a generation signal.

provenance.source: MAME source at a90e86e1, the revision the shipped binary names in its library_version. The libretro glue points -nvram_directory, -cfg_directory and -diff_directory at <save_dir>/mame/{nvram,cfg,diff} (retro_init.cpp:110-153 and :559-577); MAME then names the NVRAM file after the running machine (machine.cpp:1116-1147, written at :1178-1186) and writes both default.cfg and <machine>.cfg on every save (config.cpp:108-114). The machine's name is the ROM's own basename: the glue derives it in parsePath and passes it as the system to run (retro_init.cpp:158-207, :652). Two things the file names cannot carry. A machine with more than one NVRAM device gets a *directory* <rom_stem>/ with one file per device tag instead of a single file (machine.cpp:1125-1145), and a non-default BIOS selection appends _<n> to the name (:1121-1122). And with mame_mame_paths_enable turned on the glue sets no paths at all (retro_init.cpp:554-555), leaving MAME to take them from its own ini, which atlas does not read — that mode therefore states no file names.

groups.files_established_for: content whose file stem is spelled exactly as MAME spells the driver. The file is named after the driver, not after the ROM file: MAME 2000 matches the content's basename against its driver table case-insensitively (libretro.c:862-871, and a miss refuses the load), and then writes the table's own spelling. provenance.source: MAME 2010 source at c5b413b, the revision the shipped binary names in its library_version ('0.139 c5b413b'). The libretro glue builds <save_dir>/<core_name> from GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY, with core_name the compiled-in "mame2010" (retromain.c:36, :218), and points MAME's own path options at subdirectories of it (:239-257). MAME then names each file after the running machine, whose basename is the driver's own name (machine.c:183): NVRAM as <basename>.nv (src/emu/machine/generic.c:325-331), the score table as <basename>.hi (src/emu/hiscore.c:213 loading, :246 saving), and the configuration as both default.cfg and <basename>.cfg on every save (src/emu/config.c:133, :141-142). Two trees are stated without their files. Memory cards are 'memcard.%03d' by an index the player chooses (generic.c:476-478), shared across every game rather than keyed by one. Differencing images for CHD hard disks are named from the machine's own ROM table. Five more directories the glue creates hold nothing this question is about — ctrlr, ini, input, image and comment — and whether atlas should answer for them at all is #142. The mame-external_hiscore option chooses where the hiscore *database* is read from and does not move the save (hiscore.c:353), so it is not a governing option.

provenance.source: Virtual Jaguar source at 48096c1, the revision the shipped binary names in its library_version. On load the core takes GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY into vjs.EEPROMPath and the content's basename into vjs.romName (libretro.c:883-895), and builds two paths from them: <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.srm for the cartridge EEPROM and <save_dir>/<rom_stem>.cdrom.srm for the JagCD one (eeprom.c:99-109). Both are written whenever the game writes its EEPROM — the state machine calls EEPROMSave on a word write and on a write-all with writes enabled (eeprom.c:148-167, reached from :299-308 and :336-344), which is the ordinary in-game save rather than a shutdown path. The core also answers RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM with the same 128 bytes (libretro.c:958-965), so RetroArch writes <rom_stem>.srm as well: one path, two writers, and not the same bytes — the core stores the words as big-endian pairs (eeprom.c:42-53, mirrored by its reader at :57-65) while the frontend writes the memory block raw. Which one a file ends up holding depends on who wrote last; that is an emulator question, and it is stated here because a client comparing two machines' files will meet it. Two conditions the file names cannot carry: content whose CRC32 is 0xFDF37F47 — the Memory Track device — is exempt and gets no EEPROM files at all (eeprom.c:90-96), and content loaded without a path falls back to naming both files after the ROM's CRC32 (<CRC32>.srm, <CRC32>.cdrom.srm, eeprom.c:106-108); no launcher on either arrangement is known to load Jaguar content that way.
